name: Question 4
problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

If the matrix $A$ above is diagonalizable, find a corresponding diagonal matrix $D.$
worked_solution:
Since the matrix $A$ is triangular, its eigenvalues are the entries of the main diagonal. Therefore, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=1$ (simple root) and ${\lambda }_{2}=3$ (double root).

Let's now find the dimension of the eigenspace corresponding to each eigenvalue.

- First, we consider the simple root ${\lambda }_{1}=1.$ Since the root is simple, the dimension of the eigenspace ${V}_{1}$ corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=1$ is

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{1})=1.
$$

- Next, we consider the double root ${\lambda }_{2}=3.$ Let's find the dimension of the eigenspace ${V}_{3}$ corresponding to this eigenvalue. To do this, we row-reduce the matrix $A-3I:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-3I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). This implies that we will have $3-1=2$ linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=3.$ So, 

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{3})=2.
$$

Therefore, $A$ is diagonalizable, since

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{1})+\text{dim}({V}_{3})=1+2=3.\,✓
$$

Finally, the corresponding diagonal matrix is 

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

html:
Question 4
?

A=[151030003] If the matrix A above is diagonalizable, find a corresponding diagonal matrix D.

a
D=[3000−3000−1]
b
D=[300010001]
c
D=[300030001]
d
D=[−3000−10001]
e
A is not diagonalizable
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Since the matrix A is triangular, its eigenvalues are the entries of the main diagonal. Therefore, the eigenvalues are λ1=1 (simple root) and λ2=3 (double root).

Let's now find the dimension of the eigenspace corresponding to each eigenvalue.

  • First, we consider the simple root λ1=1. Since the root is simple, the dimension of the eigenspace V1 corresponding to λ1=1 is dim(V1)=1.
  • Next, we consider the double root λ2=3. Let's find the dimension of the eigenspace V3 corresponding to this eigenvalue. To do this, we row-reduce the matrix A−3I: A−3I=[151030003]−3[100010001]=[−251000000] In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the 1st one). This implies that we will have 3−1=2 linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to λ2=3. So, dim(V3)=2.

Therefore, A is diagonalizable, since

dim(V1)+dim(V3)=1+2=3.✓

Finally, the corresponding diagonal matrix is

D=[300030001].
